relevance_note: Case report of one girl with HA20 and a TNFAIP3 deletion ("a novel de novo 119 kb microdeletion containing only TNFAIP3"), plus a literature table (Table 1) of four previously reported HA20 patients with TNFAIP3 deletions.
method_note: Read the paper in full; a Python script assembled the JSON and copied Table 1 and Supplementary Table S1 cells by splitting the Markdown lines, and the output was checked against the tables by eye. Table 1 shows patients as columns (header row 'Location'; column 1 'This report' = the index patient, labelled 'patient' in every table; columns 2-5 are previously published patients labelled 'Table 1 column k', with the References cell copied into source_reference_in_review). Table 1 has no stacked ' / ' cells. Relatives: the father (II-1) and mother (II-2) get rows (tested; no features reported, all checklist items not reported). The grandparents had DNA extracted and appear in the pedigree figure, but the text gives no number, labels or results for them, so they get no rows. The TNFAIP3 c.305A>G (NM_001270507.2) SNP (patient A/A, mother A/G, father G/G) is described by the authors as relatively common (MAF = 0.0117) and used as a marker for the deletion; it gets no variant rows. Contradictions/notes: the deletion size is 187 kb by WES-based CNV analysis (EXCAVATOR2) and 119 kb by SNP array; the 119 kb ISCN string is recorded. Inheritance 'de novo' rests on the authors' 'de novo' plus CNV analysis of both parents (Suppl. Fig. S1 caption) and SNP array of the father; the mother's negative result is not stated separately in the text. Zygosity 'heterozygous' from 'lost the paternal allele' and 'TNFAIP3 heterozygous microdeletion'. Normal findings recorded per D-27: 'Esophagogastroduodenoscopy findings were unremarkable', 'The terminal ileum was normal', 'Her perinatal history was unremarkable' and the immunological workup with 'no apparent abnormalities' are recorded as written and exclude nothing more specific. Supplementary Table S1 (labs at 8 months; ANA at 2 months): values above the printed normal range recorded as observed (CRP, ESR, IL-6, sTNFR-1, sTNFR-2, IL-18, speckled ANA 80x vs normal <40x); 'negative' results recorded as excluded; WBC 18,060 cells/uL has no printed normal range and is not recorded. ANA patterns other than speckled were <40x (normal) and are not recorded as separate rows. Not recorded: 'Although she was afebrile' (state at 8 months, not an absence of recurrent fever); screening at 1 month 'not consistent with primary immunodeficiency, autoinflammatory disease, or hemophagocytic syndrome' (diagnostic screening, not a feature). Checklist judgments: anal/perianal ulcers counted as gastrointestinal ulcers; Table 1 column 4 'thyroiditis' is not stated as autoimmune, so 'autoimmune thyroiditis' is left not reported; Table 1 column 5 'Upper respiratory infections' and 'febrile episodes' (plural) counted as recurrent infections and recurrent fever; 'enlarged tonsil' and 'hepatosplenomegaly' not counted as lymphoproliferation. publications: n_patients_reported = 1 (the case reported first-hand); cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true only because Table 1 columns 2-5 are previously published patients; the index patient is first described here (the paper cites a ClinVar accession SCV001424911 for the deletion).
